stories.headline: Allahabad HC: Regional Rural Bank can claim Section 80P deduction
points: Allahabad HC dismissed ten Revenue appeals against Baroda Uttar Pradesh Gramin Bank for AY 2012-13 to 2016-17.
Court said Sections 22 and 32 of the RRB Act, 1976 treat such banks as cooperative societies for income-tax purposes.
It also upheld the Tribunal's view that no concealment was shown, so Section 271(1)(c) penalties could not stand.
stories.why_it_matters: Shows how a special statute can override tax circulars and why a rejected deduction claim alone may not attract penalty.
stories.source_title: Income Tax | Regional Rural Bank Eligible for Section 80P Deduction: Allahabad HC

stories.headline: Telangana HC sends GST cancellation dispute to revocation route
points: Telangana HC disposed of Aqsa Begum's petition against a GST registration cancellation order dated 9 October 2026.
Cancellation was based on Rule 21(a): business allegedly not run from the declared place, with a panchanama report cited.
Court allowed a Section 30 revocation plea with documents; authority to decide preferably within four weeks of filing.
stories.why_it_matters: Shows how GST registration cancellation and the Section 30 revocation remedy work, a common point in GST practice and compliance.
stories.source_title: Goods and Services Tax | GST Registration Revocation Application to Be Decided in Four Weeks: Telangana HC

stories.headline: Bank holidays 16-22 November: where branches will be shut
points: Per the RBI calendar, branches close 16 Nov in Patna and Ranchi for Chhath Puja, and 20 Nov in Dehradun for Igas-Bagwal.
22 November is a Sunday, so banks stay closed across India.
Branches shut, but UPI, net banking, apps, NEFT and RTGS requests stay available during holidays.
stories.why_it_matters: Bank closures affect cheque clearing, payment timing and cash flow, which accounting and compliance work often depends on.
stories.source_title: Bank holidays next week: SBI, HDFC, ICICI branches to closed on three days from 16-22 November? Check RBI calendar
check_notes: The 'Why it matters' line about cheque clearing, payment timing, cash flow and accounting/compliance work is the writer's own framing and isn't in the source. It's general commentary, not a specific factual claim.

The point that NEFT and RTGS requests 'stay available during holidays' slightly overstates the source. The source only says transfer requests can be made using NEFT/RTGS forms; it explicitly says online banking and apps stay operational on holidays, but doesn't say this about NEFT/RTGS.
